plan: Store a deep copy of the input dict as the internal tree; expose it only via deep-copying to_data().
Implement one recursive depth-first walker pattern reused by total_word_count, unresolved_markers, and outline, dispatching on item kind (note, reference, section/group).
Count note words by deleting [[?identifier]] marker tokens (replaced with a space) before applying the \b\w+\b regex; add reference word_count values directly.
Collect marker identifiers from note text via regex capture and from reference unresolved lists into a set, returned sorted.
Render the outline as the workspace title plus one line per item in list order, indented two spaces per nesting depth.

Implement move with full validation before any mutation: string-type ids, item lookup (parent list + position), destination resolution ('workspace' literal or container item), non-container rejection, subtree-id cycle check, and index range check against the destination's current length; only then pop from the old parent and insert/append into the destination.
mechanisms: recursive part-whole tree of dict nodes with section/group as the only containers
uniform kind-dispatched operations applied identically at every nesting level
recursive aggregation for total word count with marker-stripped regex word matching
set-based recursive collection of unresolved marker identifiers with sorted output
deterministic depth-first outline traversal with depth-proportional indentation
containment invariant enforced via subtree-id set (self plus descendants) cycle check
atomic move: validate-everything-then-mutate so failed moves leave the tree untouched
